title: ATLAS Lean Reference Readout

canonical_node.axiom: ATLAS is an external reference corpus for Lean proof patterns and project structure, not canon evidence for Theophysics claims.
definitions: ATLAS: autoformalized Lean 4 textbook mathematics library, machine-generated, ongoing, with some sorry-backed declarations.
Reference corpus: a body of examples used for pattern-matching and structural guidance, not for truth-bearing claims.
Canon evidence: material that directly supports the truth of Theophysics axioms or derived claims.
derivation: ATLAS contains 2654 Lean files across 26 book/domain folders, with report.json and targets.yaml files.
Its own reports indicate some declarations are sorry-backed, meaning not all proofs are complete.
Therefore ATLAS is useful for layout and proof-review categories, but cannot serve as proof of Theophysics claims.
The document explicitly states it is not canon evidence.
canonical_node.action: Use ATLAS as an external reference for Lean project organization, proof-review metadata, dependency reports, and idiomatic Lean/mathlib patterns. Do not cite ATLAS as evidence for Theophysics truth claims.
boundary: Does not assert any mathematical theorem as true for Theophysics.
Does not provide formal proofs for Theophysics axioms.
Does not replace the need for independent verification of any Theophysics claim.
test: Check that ATLAS is referenced only for structural or idiomatic guidance, not as proof of any Theophysics claim.
Verify that any use of ATLAS in Theophysics documents is labeled as external reference, not canon evidence.
Ensure that sorry-backed declarations in ATLAS are not treated as completed proofs.

dg1_dependencies: Local repository at D:\GitHub\atlas-lean (moved to G:\GitHub\atlas-lean)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reference corpus for Lean project layout, proof-review metadata, and idiomatic patterns, enabling structured guidance for Lean specialists without claiming Theophysics truth.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the distinction between external reference and canon evidence, preventing ATLAS from being misused as proof of Theophysics claims.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the Lean specialist loses a concrete reference for project organization and proof-review patterns, but no Theophysics axiom or derived claim is invalidated.

classification.recommended_atom_action: quarantine as external reference; do not promote to canon evidence

overstatement_risks: Treating ATLAS as proof of Theophysics claims
Assuming all ATLAS proofs are complete despite sorry declarations
Using ATLAS as a source of axioms rather than patterns
kill_conditions: If ATLAS is cited as evidence for a Theophysics truth claim
If sorry-backed declarations are presented as completed proofs
If ATLAS is copied wholesale into canon without external-reference labeling
risk.lean_target: A Lean project structure and proof-review metadata schema that mirrors ATLAS's targets.yaml and report.json, but with explicit separation of theorem statement quality from proof completion.

plain_summary: ATLAS is a large autoformalized Lean library useful as a reference for Lean project organization and proof-review patterns, but it is explicitly not canon evidence for Theophysics. It must be used only as an external reference, never as proof of Theophysics claims.
